title.en: Critical points and the second derivative test

summary: Classify stationary points on a surface from the discriminant, and show the inconclusive case as a real outcome.
objective: Build a surface where I can find stationary points and see the discriminant classify each as a maximum, minimum, saddle or inconclusive case.
intent_signals: Show why a point on a surface is a saddle rather than a maximum.
Classify the stationary points of a function of two variables.
example_prompts: Build a surface with marked critical points classified by the second derivative test.
Show a case where the second derivative test is inconclusive.
negative_signals: Not an optimiser: this recipe classifies points, it does not search for optima.
Not a claim about global extrema; only local behaviour is classified.
not_for: Not an optimiser: this recipe classifies points, it does not search for optima.
Not a claim about global extrema; only local behaviour is classified.

entities.name: Height surface
entities.guidance: Sample the function on a regular indexed mesh with equal horizontal scales and a visible zero plane.

entities.name: Critical point markers
entities.guidance: Mark each stationary point with its classification label and the numeric discriminant value, not with colour alone.

entities.name: Local probe
entities.guidance: Provide two orthogonal section curves through the selected point so a saddle can be seen falling in one direction and rising in the other.

state_contract.model: An analytic function with analytic first and second partial derivatives, a set of stationary points, the discriminant at each and the resulting classification including an explicit inconclusive case.
state_contract.authority: The analytic derivatives are authoritative; mesh normals and visual curvature are illustrations and never decide a classification.
actions: Select a critical point and read its discriminant and classification.
Rotate the two section planes through the selected point.
Switch to a function whose discriminant is zero at a stationary point.
Reset the function, selection and camera.

invariants: A point is only labelled critical when both first partial derivatives vanish, within a stated tolerance.
A zero discriminant is reported as inconclusive rather than pushed into a nearby class.
The tangent plane at a critical point is horizontal in every displayed section.
motion_guidance: Animate the section plane sweeping around the point so the up and down directions of a saddle are found by the viewer, not asserted.
Avoid animating the surface itself; the function is fixed while classification is inspected.
known_limits: Only twice-differentiable functions of two variables are covered.
Mesh resolution can hide narrow features; classification comes from analytic derivatives, not from the mesh.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: A point is a critical point of a function of two variables when both first partial derivatives vanish there or one of them fails to exist.
claims.scope: Definition for functions defined on an open set as cited.

claims.statement: With discriminant D equal to f_xx times f_yy minus the square of f_xy, D greater than zero with positive f_xx gives a local minimum, D greater than zero with negative f_xx gives a local maximum, D less than zero gives a saddle point, and D equal to zero is inconclusive.
claims.scope: Evaluated at a stationary point of a function whose first and second partial derivatives are continuous on a neighbourhood of that point; D = 0 is genuinely inconclusive, and a floating-point D near zero is reported as numerically inconclusive rather than as exactly zero.

object_craft.structure: Indexed quad mesh with enough resolution near marked points that a saddle does not disappear between samples.
object_craft.material: Matte surface with restrained elevation shading; keep the zero plane visible and translucent.
object_craft.articulation: None. The surface is regenerated only when the function changes.

object_craft.structure: Distinct marker shapes per class plus a leader line to a text plate carrying the discriminant value.
object_craft.material: Opaque label plates so text stays readable over any part of the surface.
object_craft.articulation: Markers rebuild when the function changes and remain anchored to their domain coordinates.

physical_contract.scope: Analytic evaluation and presentation; nothing moves under physical rules.
checks: Every marked point reports vanishing first derivatives within the tolerance.
A function with a degenerate stationary point reports the inconclusive case.
